newsitem.title: CYPRUS: Greek jets will respond swiftly to Turks - minister.
newsitem.headline: Greek jets will respond swiftly to Turks - minister.

text.p: Greece's Defence Minister Akis Tsohatzopoulos said on Sunday Greek fighter jets would be swift in their response to any Turkish offensive in divided Cyprus.
"Be sure that when needed, they will require the minimum time to be close to Cyprus," Tsohatzopoulos told a news conference at the end of a four-day visit to the eastern Mediterranean island.
Cyprus has a common defence pact with Greece since November 1993. Both governments say it is aimed at thwarting a further offensive by Turkey, which occupied one third of the island in 1974.
According to some estimates, Turkish fighter jets can be over the island, 50 km (32 miles) south off the Turkish coast, in around six minutes. Greece is 550 km (350 miles) away.
"Geography has its own logic. We cannot ignore it," said Tsohatzopoulos. "This issue is adressed by the common defence pact."
Tsohatzopoulos said the defence pact between the two countries provided them with "clear, specific abilities" to deal with any Turkish attack.

Turkey invaded north Cyprus in 1974 in the wake of a brief Greek Cypriot coup engineered by the military ruling in Greece at the time. Some 30,000 Turkish troops are stationed in northern Cyprus, declared a Turkish Cypriot breakaway state in 1983 but recognised only by Ankara.
